disclaimer: Agricultural chemical applications must strictly adhere to product label directions, Central Insecticides Board & Registration Committee (CIBRC) approvals, and regional agricultural extension recommendations. Always consult a certified local agronomist before foliar chemical sprays.

symptoms: Dark brown circular spots with concentric target-like rings on older lower leaves
Chlorotic yellow halo surrounding necrotic lesion borders
Premature defoliation starting from bottom canopy upwards
Dark sunken leathery stem and fruit collar rot near calyx
causes: High relative humidity (>75%) coupled with moderate temperatures (24-29°C)
Overcrowded planting and poor bottom-canopy aeration

immediate_actions: Physically prune and destroy lower infected leaves showing concentric lesions to prevent upward spore splash
Switch immediately from overhead sprinkling to drip or furrow irrigation to keep foliage dry
Sanitize pruning shears between plants using a 10% sodium hypochlorite solution
cultural_control: Maintain optimal plant spacing (60 x 45 cm) and stake tomato vines to improve air circulation
Apply clean straw or plastic mulch around plant bases to create a physical barrier against soil-borne spores
Implement a 3-year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops (e.g., legumes, cereals)
mechanical_control: Erect protective rain shelters or poly-tunnels during monsoon seasons to minimize direct foliar rain splash
Remove and deeply bury or burn all crop residues immediately after harvest
biological_control: Foliar spray of Trichoderma harzianum or Bacillus subtilis (10 g/L) during early vegetative growth
Apply 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) as a natural anti-sporulant at 10-day intervals
chemical_control: Preventative: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.0-2.5 g/L or Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2.0 g/L at the first appearance of lower leaf spots
Curative (if severity high): Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC @ 1.0 ml/L or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 1.0 ml/L. Observe strict 7-day Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI).
prevention: Procure certified disease-free seeds or treat seeds with Carbendazim 50% WP @ 2 g/kg seed before nursery sowing
Adopt resistant or tolerant tomato hybrids (e.g., Arka Rakshak, Arka Abhed)
monitoring: Inspect lower leaves twice weekly during humid or cloudy weather cycles
Deploy spore traps in commercial open-field blocks to monitor early airborne conidia load
management.expert_escalation: Escalate to extension officer if lesions rapidly progress past mid-canopy within 48 hours or fruit collar rot exceeds 15%.

symptoms: Water-soaked pale green irregular lesions turning rapidly dark brown and necrotic
Delicate white cottony/downy fungal sporulation visible on leaf undersides under high humidity
Rapid blighting of leaves, petioles, and green fruits with dark greasy firm rot
causes: Cool night temperatures (10-15°C) paired with warm humid days (18-22°C)
Extended periods of cloudiness, mist, and persistent leaf wetness (>90% RH)

immediate_actions: Roguing and deep burial of heavily blighted plants to curb rapid field epidemic spread
Cease all sprinkler and overhead watering immediately
cultural_control: Avoid planting adjacent to potato fields
Ensure wide ridge planting with excellent furrow drainage to eliminate standing puddles
mechanical_control: Destroy volunteer potato and solanaceous weed hosts (e.g., Solanum nigrum) along field borders
biological_control: Prophylactic foliar application of Pseudomonas fluorescens (10 g/L) before weather-driven blight outbreaks
chemical_control: Preventative: Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5-3.0 g/L or Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L
Systemic Curative: Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.0 g/L. Rotate fungicide modes of action to prevent resistance.
prevention: Plant resistant hybrids and ensure proper field site selection with maximum solar exposure
monitoring: Daily canopy scouting during foggy or continuous rainy spells
management.expert_escalation: Immediate escalation required if white downy sporulation appears on more than 5% of field plants.

symptoms: Concentric target-board brown spots on older foliage
Yellowing and senescence of infected leaflets
Sunken dark circular corky dry rot lesions on harvested tubers
causes: Alternating wet and dry periods during tuber bulking stage

immediate_actions: Maintain uniform soil moisture; avoid severe moisture stress between irrigation cycles
Remove and destroy lower diseased foliage during field inter-culture
cultural_control: Balanced NPK fertilization; avoid premature nitrogen starvation during tuber expansion
3-year crop rotation with non-host cereal or pulse crops
mechanical_control: Ensure full tuber hill coverage (proper earthing-up) to prevent conidia reaching developing tubers
biological_control: Tuber treatment with Trichoderma viride @ 5 g/kg seed tuber prior to planting
chemical_control: Foliar spray of Propineb 70% WP @ 2.0 g/L or Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L at first symptom onset
Curative: Difenoconazole 25% EC @ 0.5-1.0 ml/L or Pyraclostrobin 20% WG @ 1.0 g/L
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed tubers from verified seed producers (e.g., CPRI Jalandhar/Shimla)
monitoring: Scout lower canopy at 5-day intervals following canopy closure
management.expert_escalation: Escalate if foliar blight leads to premature canopy collapse prior to 70 days after planting.

symptoms: Linear parallel stripes of bright yellow to orange-yellow powdery pustules (uredinia) along leaf blades
Yellow dust easily dislodged on fingers or clothing upon contact
Rapid leaf chlorosis and drying under cool windy weather leading to shriveled grains
causes: Cool temperatures (10-15°C) and high humidity / dew in North-Western Plains and sub-mountainous tracts (Punjab, Haryana, MP)
Susceptible varieties sown across large contiguous belts

immediate_actions: Identify and demarcate yellow rust focus patches in the field immediately
Initiate spot spray on focus patches and surrounding 5-meter buffer to prevent airborne epidemic
cultural_control: Timely sowing within recommended sowing window (first fortnight of November)
Avoid excessive vegetative nitrogen fertilization which fosters lush susceptible tissue
mechanical_control: Eradicate wild grass alternate/collateral hosts along water channels and field boundaries
biological_control: No commercial biocontrol agent replaces chemical intervention during active yellow rust outbreaks
chemical_control: Single foliar spray of Propiconazole 25% EC (Tilt) @ 1.0 ml/L (200 ml in 200 L water/acre) or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 1.0 ml/L at first appearance of yellow stripes. Repeat in 15 days if cloudy cool weather persists.
prevention: Sow certified rust-resistant wheat varieties (e.g., HD 3086, DBW 187, DBW 222, PBW 824, PBW 869)
Avoid growing banned or highly susceptible obsolete varieties (e.g., HD 2967 in stripe-rust prone zones)
monitoring: Scout fields weekly starting early January, focusing on low-lying shaded field corners
management.expert_escalation: Immediate mandatory reporting to district agricultural officer / Krishi Vigyan Kendra upon first verified stripe rust focus.

symptoms: Spindle-shaped elliptical lesions with pointed ends, greyish-white centers and reddish-brown margins on leaves
Blackish necrotic lesions on panicle nodes and neck (Neck Blast) causing complete panicle breakage and chaffy grains
causes: Intermittent rains, cloudy weather, high relative humidity (>90%), and night temperatures of 20-24°C
Excessive basal or top-dressed nitrogen fertilizer

immediate_actions: Suspend top-dressing of nitrogen fertilizers immediately during active blast development
Drain excess standing water temporarily and maintain shallow saturated soil
cultural_control: Split application of nitrogen in 3-4 doses with adequate potassium top-dressing
Avoid dense seedling planting and ensure optimum hill spacing (20 x 15 cm)
mechanical_control: Destroy infected straw piles and stubbles after harvest to reduce overwintering perithecia
biological_control: Seed treatment and foliar spray of Pseudomonas fluorescens (Pf-1) @ 10 g/L or 2.5 kg/ha in 500 L water
chemical_control: Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6 g/L (120 g/acre) or Isoprothiolane 40% EC @ 1.5 ml/L or Trifloxystrobin 25% + Tebuconazole 50% WG @ 0.4 g/L at early tillering and panicle emergence stage.
prevention: Seed treatment with Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 2 g/kg seed or Carbendazim 50% WP @ 2 g/kg seed
Adopt blast-resistant rice cultivars suited for regional belts
monitoring: Regular inspection of nursery beds and tillering fields during cool foggy mornings
management.expert_escalation: Escalate immediately if neck blast symptoms appear during early grain filling (milking) stage.

entries.disease_name: Cotton Bacterial Blight / Angular Leaf Spot
symptoms: Angular water-soaked spots bounded by leaf veinlets on underside of leaves turning brown to black
Black arm: Dark elongated cankers girdling stems and branches causing branch snapping
Dark oily water-soaked spots on young developing bolls leading to boll rot and stained lint
causes: Warm humid weather (28-34°C with >80% RH) with high wind-driven rains
Infected seed transmission and volunteer cotton ratoon plants

immediate_actions: Prune severely affected black-arm branches during dry afternoon hours and destroy
Avoid sprinkler irrigation which facilitates bacterial splash
cultural_control: Crop rotation with non-malvaceous crops (e.g., maize, sorghum, pulses)
Delinting of cotton seeds with concentrated sulfuric acid (100 ml/kg seed) to kill seed-coat bacteria
mechanical_control: Collect and burn all infected cotton stalks and post-harvest debris
biological_control: Seed treatment with Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10 g/kg seed
chemical_control: Foliar spray with Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5 g/L mixed with Streptocycline (Streptomycin sulphate + Tetracycline) @ 100 mg/L (1 g in 10 L water). Repeat after 15 days if rainy weather continues.
prevention: Plant acid-delinted certified Bt and non-Bt cotton seeds
Select bacterial blight resistant or tolerant hybrids
monitoring: Inspect lower leaves of young plants 30-45 days after sowing following early monsoon showers
management.expert_escalation: Escalate if black arm stem girdling exceeds 10% of main stems across the field.

symptoms: Rosetted flowers that fail to open properly due to larval petal webbing
Tiny entry holes in green bolls that heal and become invisible from outside
Burrowed seeds, stained unopenable locules (bad kapis), and premature boll dropping
Pink larvae (10-12 mm) feeding inside mature bolls with characteristic exit holes

immediate_actions: Handpick and destroy rosetted flowers and dropped green bolls from the field
Install pheromone traps immediately to identify adult moth peak emergence
cultural_control: Strict termination of cotton crop by December/January; avoid ratoon cotton cultivation
Deep summer ploughing to expose diapausing larvae and pupae in soil to predators and sun
mechanical_control: Install 8-10 Delta Pheromone Traps with Phero-lure per hectare for continuous monitoring (ETL: 8 moths/trap/night for 3 consecutive nights)
Deploy light traps during evening hours to capture nocturnal adult moths
biological_control: Release egg parasitoid Trichogramma bactrae @ 1.5 lakh/ha at weekly intervals starting at flower initiation (45-50 DAS)
Foliar spray of Beauveria bassiana (1 x 10^8 CFU/g) @ 5 g/L during evening hours
chemical_control: At ETL (10% green boll damage or 8 moths/trap/night): Spray Profenofos 50% EC @ 2.0 ml/L or Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG @ 0.4 g/L (80 g/acre) or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.3 ml/L (60 ml/acre). Alternate insecticide chemical groups.
prevention: Ensure timely regional sowing to escape late-season pink bollworm population peaks
monitoring: Destructive sampling of 20 green bolls per acre weekly between 60 to 120 days after sowing
management.expert_escalation: Escalate to agronomist if live pink larvae are found inside more than 10% of green bolls.

entries.source_name: ICAR-CICR Nagpur & Commissionerate of Agriculture MH

symptoms: Elongated papery transparent patches (window panes) on leaves caused by young larvae
Large irregular ragged shot holes on expanding leaves with abundant sawdust-like coarse frass inside leaf whorl
Larva has inverted Y-shape mark on head capsule and four raised black dots arranged in a square on the 8th abdominal segment

immediate_actions: Apply dry sand or wood ash mixed with lime (9:1) directly into affected leaf whorls to desiccate young larvae
Handpick and crush conspicuous egg masses covered with grey scales and early instar larval clusters
cultural_control: Intercropping maize with legumes (cowpea, pigeonpea, or soybean) to enhance natural predator biodiversity
Avoid staggered planting in adjacent plots; practice community-wide synchronized sowing
mechanical_control: Install FAW pheromone traps @ 10-12 traps/ha for monitoring and mass trapping
biological_control: Egg parasitoid Trichogramma pretiosum or Telenomus remus @ 50,000/acre at weekly intervals
Whorl application of Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) kurstaki @ 2 g/L or Metarhizium anisopliae @ 5 g/L
chemical_control: Early Whorl Stage (ETL: 5-10% damaged plants): Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.4 ml/L (80 ml/acre) directed straight into leaf whorls, or Spinetoram 11.7% SC @ 0.5 ml/L (100 ml/acre), or Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG @ 0.4 g/L (80 g/acre).
prevention: Seed treatment with Cyantraniliprole 19.8% + Thiamethoxam 19.8% FS @ 6 ml/kg seed protects young seedlings for first 20 days
monitoring: Scout 20 consecutive plants across 5 spots in a 'W' pattern from seedling emergence through tasseling
management.expert_escalation: Escalate if whorl damage exceeds 10% in vegetative maize or larvae begin burrowing directly into emerging cobs.
